name: xargs
summary: Turns standard input into arguments for a command.
description: Some commands, such as rm, do not read standard input: they expect arguments. xargs bridges the gap: it reads words (one per line or separated by spaces) and adds them as arguments to the command that follows it, grouping as many as it can. With -I, each item is inserted where you say. For file names containing spaces, combine find -print0 and xargs -0.

options.description: Replaces this string with each item and runs one command per item (often -I {}).
At most N arguments per run of the command.
Items are separated by a null byte (with find -print0): handles spaces in names.
Runs up to N commands in parallel.
Asks for confirmation before each run.
Prints each command before running it.
Does not run the command if the input is empty.

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: Command to run with the items read (echo by default), followed by its own options.

examples.explanation: Deletes every .tmp file found by find.
Resizes the images, names with spaces included, 4 at a time.
Downloads each URL in the file, one command per URL.

examples.output:
echo a
a
echo b
b
echo c
c

dangerNote: Combined with rm, xargs acts on everything it receives. Check the list first (replace rm with echo), and use -0 for names containing spaces.
